newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt rounds up 1,500 after village massacre.
newsitem.headline: Egypt rounds up 1,500 after village massacre.

text.p: Egyptian police have rounded up for questioning more than 1,500 people after suspected Moslem militants massacred 14 people in a southern hamlet last week, security sources said on Monday.

They said police in Qena governorate were gathering any information about three wanted members of the militant Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) suspected of gunning down the villagers in Ezbet Dawoud on Thursday and then attacking a Cairo-bound train.
Police identified the suspects as Gama'a members Anwar Hamed, Abdel Razek Atta and Mahmoud el-Farshouti. The group has denied in a faxed statement that it was behind the attack.
The sources said the men rampaged through the village, shooting passers-by before heading for Nag Hammadi, some 450 km (280 miles) south of Cairo, and firing at a train.
Police identified eight of the dead as Coptic Christians, one of the groups targeted by the Gama'a in its campaign to topple the government.

The militants have also shot at tourists, particularly on the line south from Cairo, in their drive to sabotage Egypt's economy, which is dependent on foreign revenue. Other targets have been policemen and government ministers.
More than 1,000 people have been killed in political violence since the militants took up arms in 1992.
